newsitem.title: JAPAN: Oversupply keeps Tokyo naphtha spreads in contango.
newsitem.headline: Oversupply keeps Tokyo naphtha spreads in contango.

text.p: Naphtha spreads remained in contango in Tokyo due to a persistent supply surplus in near-term supplies, traders said on Monday.
"There are at least two distressed naphtha vessels floating off the coast (of Chiba)," one trader said. "In the second half of June, we are likely to have as many as four of them."
He also said most distressed vessels were from the West.
Bids for the one-month spread from first-half August were heard at minus $2.00 with no offers. It was traded once at minus $1.50 and again at minus $1.80 on Friday.
Also on Friday, second-half July/second-half August changed hands at minus $2.20.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half August hovered just above the $200 per tonne, pulled down by a sharp fall in crude prices on Friday. It was quoted at around $206.50/207.00 in late Friday trading.
Naphtha activity remained lacklustre with traders unsure of market direction, traders said.
"Both buyers and sellers are a little bit hesitant to show where they are today," one trader said.
